        border-left:3px solid var(--cyan);padding-left:10px}
  code{background:#0c1226;padding:1px 5px;border-radius:4px;color:var(--green);font-size:12.5px}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="wrap">
  <h1>The Pythagorean Star Map Explorer</h1>
  <p class="sub">
    Every primitive Pythagorean triple comes from a <em>seed</em> (m, n) with 0 < n < m,
    gcd(m, n) = 1 and m + n odd, through a = m² − n², b = 2mn, c = m² + n².
    Plot the seed as the point z(m, n) = (n + i)/m of the hyperbolic upper half-plane and the
    triples arrange themselves into fans of perfectly straight lines. Pick a boundary rational
    p/q below: the highlighted rays are the level sets of the <em>star charge</em>
    k = qn − pm, and every node on one of them lies at the same hyperbolic distance
    arsinh(|k|/q) from the vertical geodesic over p/q.
  </p>

  <div class="layout">
    <div>
      <canvas id="cv" width="1500" height="820"></canvas>
      <div class="note" id="story"></div>
    </div>

    <div class="panel">
      <h2>Boundary point</h2>
      <div class="chips" id="fanChips"></div>
      <label>custom numerator p <span id="pOut"></span></label>
      <input type="range" id="pIn" min="0" max="12" step="1" value="1"/>
      <label>custom denominator q <span id="qOut"></span></label>
      <input type="range" id="qIn" min="1" max="12" step="1" value="3"/>

      <h2 style="margin-top:16px">Detail</h2>
      <label>largest seed m ≤ <span id="mOut"></span></label>
      <input type="range" id="mIn" min="30" max="400" step="10" value="180"/>
      <label>rays drawn, |k| ≤ <span id="kOut"></span></label>
      <input type="range" id="kIn" min="1" max="60" step="1" value="25"/>

      <div class="toggles">
        <label style="margin:0"><input type="checkbox" id="tCirc"/> hyperbolic circles</label>
        <label style="margin:0"><input type="checkbox" id="tSpine" checked/> Pell spine</label>
        <label style="margin:0"><input type="checkbox" id="tColour" checked/> colour by charge</label>
      </div>

      <h2 style="margin-top:16px">The laws, live</h2>
      <div class="read" id="readout"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
const cv = document.getElementById('cv'), ctx = cv.getContext('2d');
const W = cv.width, H = cv.height;
const YMAX = 0.55;                    // top of the visible strip, in Im z
const PAD = {l:56, r:22, t:22, b:52};

function gcd(a,b){a=Math.abs(a);b=Math.abs(b);while(b){[a,b]=[b,a%b];}return a;}
function isSeed(m,n){return 0<n && n<m && gcd(m,n)===1 && ((m+n)%2===1);}
function totient(k){let r=k,x=k;for(let d=2;d*d<=x;d++){if(x%d===0){while(x%d===0)x/=d;r-=r/d;}}if(x>1)r-=r/x;return Math.round(r);}
function starGap(p,q){return ((p+q)%2===1)?1:2;}

const state = {p:1,q:3,mmax:180,kmax:25,circles:false,spine:true,colour:true};

// ---------- coordinate transforms ----------
function X(x){return PAD.l + x*(W-PAD.l-PAD.r);}
function Y(y){return H-PAD.b - (y/YMAX)*(H-PAD.t-PAD.b);}

// ---------- node cache ----------
let nodes=[];
function buildNodes(){
  nodes=[];
  for(let m=2;m<=state.mmax;m++)
    for(let n=1;n<m;n++)
      if(isSeed(m,n)) nodes.push([m,n]);
}

const PALETTE=['#4cc9f0','#57cc99','#ffa62b','#f72585','#b892ff','#ffd166','#ff5d8f','#7ee8fa'];

function draw(){
  const p=state.p,q=state.q,tip=p/q,gap=starGap(p,q);
  ctx.fillStyle='#060a16';ctx.fillRect(0,0,W,H);

  // axes
  ctx.strokeStyle='#233055';ctx.lineWidth=1;
  ctx.beginPath();ctx.moveTo(PAD.l,Y(0));ctx.lineTo(W-PAD.r,Y(0));ctx.stroke();
  ctx.fillStyle='#93a0c0';ctx.font='13px system-ui';
  for(let i=0;i<=10;i++){const x=i/10;
    ctx.fillText(x.toFixed(1), X(x)-10, Y(0)+22);
    ctx.strokeStyle='#16203c';ctx.beginPath();ctx.moveTo(X(x),Y(0));ctx.lineTo(X(x),Y(YMAX));ctx.stroke();}
  ctx.fillText('Re z = n/m', W/2-38, H-14);
  ctx.save();ctx.translate(16,H/2+42);ctx.rotate(-Math.PI/2);ctx.fillText('Im z = 1/m',0,0);ctx.restore();

  // the rays of the chosen star
  for(let k=-state.kmax;k<=state.kmax;k++){
    if(gap===2 && k%2===0) continue;
    const xEnd = tip + (k/q)*YMAX;
    ctx.strokeStyle = (k===0)?'#ffffff55':(PALETTE[Math.abs(k)%PALETTE.length]+'44');
    ctx.lineWidth = (Math.abs(k)<=1)?1.6:0.8;
    ctx.beginPath();ctx.moveTo(X(tip),Y(0));ctx.lineTo(X(xEnd),Y(YMAX));ctx.stroke();
  }

  // hyperbolic circles about i
  if(state.circles){
    ctx.strokeStyle='#80ed9955';ctx.lineWidth=1;ctx.setLineDash([5,5]);
    for(let R=0.9;R<5.2;R+=0.45){
      const ch=Math.cosh(R),sh=Math.sinh(R);let started=false;ctx.beginPath();
      for(let t=0;t<=Math.PI;t+=Math.PI/400){
        const m=ch+sh*Math.cos(t),n=sh*Math.sin(t);
        if(m<0.6) {started=false;continue;}
        const x=n/m,y=1/m;if(y>YMAX){started=false;continue;}
        if(!started){ctx.moveTo(X(x),Y(y));started=true;}else ctx.lineTo(X(x),Y(y));
      }
      ctx.stroke();
    }
    ctx.setLineDash([]);
  }

  // nodes, coloured by |charge| at the chosen star
  for(const [m,n] of nodes){
    const x=n/m,y=1/m;if(y>YMAX)continue;
    const k=q*n-p*m;
    const r=Math.max(1.0, 26/Math.pow(m,0.62));
    if(state.colour){
      const a = Math.max(0.18, 1 - Math.abs(k)/(state.kmax+1));
      ctx.fillStyle = (Math.abs(k)<=state.kmax)
        ? PALETTE[Math.abs(k)%PALETTE.length] + Math.floor(a*255).toString(16).padStart(2,'0')
        : '#ffd16633';
    } else ctx.fillStyle='#ffd166cc';
    ctx.beginPath();ctx.arc(X(x),Y(y),r,0,2*Math.PI);ctx.fill();
  }

  // Pell spine
  if(state.spine){
    let m=2,n=1;ctx.strokeStyle='#ffffff';ctx.lineWidth=2;ctx.beginPath();ctx.moveTo(X(n/m),Y(1/m));
    for(let i=0;i<10;i++){const M=2*m+n;n=m;m=M;if(1/m<=YMAX)ctx.lineTo(X(n/m),Y(1/m));}
    ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle='#ffffff';ctx.font='13px system-ui';
    ctx.fillText('Pell spine: steps → log(1+√2) = 0.8814', X(0.52), Y(0.44));
  }

  // tip marker
  ctx.fillStyle='#ffffff';ctx.beginPath();ctx.arc(X(tip),Y(0),5,0,2*Math.PI);ctx.fill();
  ctx.font='15px system-ui';ctx.fillText(`${p}/${q}`, X(tip)-10, Y(0)+40);
}

function readout(){
  const p=state.p,q=state.q,gap=starGap(p,q),delta=gap/q;
  const bothOdd = (p%2===1 && q%2===1);
  // census of the unit ray and of a chosen charge
  const kdemo = (gap===2)?3:2;
  const predicted = (bothOdd || kdemo%2===0) ? 2*totient(kdemo) : totient(kdemo);
  let onRay=0, minW=Infinity, tipNodes=0;
  for(const [m,n] of nodes){const k=q*n-p*m;if(Math.abs(k)===1)onRay++;if(k===0)tipNodes++;
    const w=Math.abs(k)/q;if(w<minW)minW=w;}
  const html = `
   <div class="kv"><span>star charge</span><span>k = ${q}n − ${p}m</span></div>
   <div class="kv"><span>parity of p+q</span><span>${(p+q)%2===1?'odd':'even (p,q both odd)'}</span></div>
   <div class="kv"><span>charges realised</span><span>${bothOdd?'odd k only':'every integer k'}</span></div>
   <div class="kv"><span>charge spacing</span><span>${gap}</span></div>
   <div class="kv"><span>resolution δ = gap/q</span><span>${delta.toFixed(4)}</span></div>
   <div class="kv"><span>visible (δ ≥ 2/5)?</span><span>${delta>=0.4-1e-12?'YES':'no'}</span></div>
   <div class="kv"><span>node on the geodesic</span><span>${tipNodes?`(m,n) = (${q},${p})`:'none'}</span></div>
   <div class="kv"><span>nodes on a unit ray (m ≤ ${state.mmax})</span><span>${onRay}</span></div>
   <div class="kv"><span>census of charge ${kdemo} per 2k window</span><span>${predicted} = ${(bothOdd||kdemo%2===0)?'2φ':'φ'}(${kdemo})</span></div>
   <div class="kv"><span>width of the nearest ray</span><span>arsinh(${minW.toFixed(3)}) = ${Math.asinh(minW).toFixed(4)}</span></div>`;
  document.getElementById('readout').innerHTML = html;

  const story = bothOdd
   ? `Both <code>p = ${p}</code> and <code>q = ${q}</code> are odd, so every charge
      <code>k = ${q}n − ${p}m</code> is forced to be odd: half of the pencil is empty and the
      surviving rays are spaced <code>2/${q}</code> apart in sinh of their hyperbolic width.
      Each surviving ray is correspondingly twice as bright — a window of <code>2k</code>
      positions along it carries <code>2φ(k)</code> nodes.`
   : `Here <code>p + q</code> is odd, so <em>every</em> integer charge occurs, including
      <code>k = 0</code>: the geodesic over <code>${p}/${q}</code> itself carries the single node
      <code>(m,n) = (${q},${p})</code>. The rays are packed <code>1/${q}</code> apart in sinh, twice
      as finely as at a both-odd point, and each odd-charge ray is only half as bright,
      <code>φ(k)</code> nodes per window of <code>2k</code>.`;
  document.getElementById('story').innerHTML = story +
    `<br/><br/>Resolution here is <code>δ = ${gap}/${q} = ${(gap/q).toFixed(4)}</code>` +
    (gap/q>=0.4-1e-12
      ? ` — above the empirical visibility threshold <code>2/5</code>, so this fan is one of the
         six you can actually see: <code>0, 1/5, 1/3, 1/2, 3/5, 1</code>.`
      : ` — below <code>2/5</code>, so this fan blurs into the background. Compare
         <code>1/4</code> (δ = 0.25, invisible) with <code>1/5</code> (δ = 0.4, visible): the even
         denominator forfeits the parity bonus.`);
}

function refresh(){buildNodes();draw();readout();}

// ---------- controls ----------
const FANS=[[0,1],[1,5],[1,3],[1,2],[3,5],[1,1],[1,4],[2,5],[2,3],[3,7]];
const chips=document.getElementById('fanChips');
FANS.forEach(([p,q])=>{
  const b=document.createElement('button');
  b.className='chip'+(starGap(p,q)/q>=0.4?'':' faint');
  b.textContent=`${p}/${q}`;
  b.onclick=()=>{state.p=p;state.q=q;
    document.getElementById('pIn').value=p;document.getElementById('qIn').value=q;
    syncLabels();markChips();refresh();};
  chips.appendChild(b);
});
function markChips(){[...chips.children].forEach((b,i)=>{
  const [p,q]=FANS[i];b.classList.toggle('on', p===state.p&&q===state.q);});}

function syncLabels(){
  document.getElementById('pOut').textContent='= '+state.p;
  document.getElementById('qOut').textContent='= '+state.q;
  document.getElementById('mOut').textContent=state.mmax;
  document.getElementById('kOut').textContent=state.kmax;
}
function bindRange(id,key,after){
  const el=document.getElementById(id);
  el.oninput=()=>{state[key]=parseInt(el.value,10);
    if(key==='p'||key==='q'){ if(state.q<1)state.q=1; if(state.p>state.q)state.p=state.q; }
    if(after)after();syncLabels();markChips();refresh();};
}
bindRange('pIn','p');bindRange('qIn','q');bindRange('mIn','mmax');bindRange('kIn','kmax');
document.getElementById('tCirc').onchange=e=>{state.circles=e.target.checked;draw();};
document.getElementById('tSpine').onchange=e=>{state.spine=e.target.checked;draw();};
document.getElementById('tColour').onchange=e=>{state.colour=e.target.checked;draw();};

// click on the canvas near the axis to jump to the nearest visible fan
cv.onclick=(ev)=>{
  const rect=cv.getBoundingClientRect();
  const x=((ev.clientX-rect.left)*(W/rect.width)-PAD.l)/(W-PAD.l-PAD.r);
  let best=null;
  for(let q=1;q<=12;q++)for(let p=0;p<=q;p++){
    if(gcd(p,q)!==1)continue;
    const score=Math.abs(p/q-x)+0.02*q/starGap(p,q);
    if(!best||score<best[0])best=[score,p,q];
  }
  if(best){state.p=best[1];state.q=best[2];
    document.getElementById('pIn').value=state.p;document.getElementById('qIn').value=state.q;
    syncLabels();markChips();refresh();}
};

syncLabels();markChips();refresh();
</script>
</body>
</html>
"
    },
    {
      "title": "Charge, Resolution and Brightness Laboratory",
      "description": "A hands-on verification of the totient brightness law. Choose a boundary rational p/q, a charge k and a window offset; the widget computes Bezout integers x, y with qx - py = 1, displays the resulting ray parametrisation (m,n) = (qA + yk, pA + xk), and then scans the window of 2k consecutive ray parameters one by one, tabulating for each the coordinates, their greatest common divisor, the parity of m+n and whether the point is a genuine Pythagorean seed. The count is compared live against the predicted value -- 2*phi(k) at a both-odd star or for an even charge, phi(k) = phi(2k) in the mixed regime, and zero for the forbidden even charges at a both-odd star -- and sliding the window offset demonstrates that the census is independent of where the window begins. A chart plots the two theoretical density curves phi(k)/k and phi(k)/(2k) against charge, overlaid with the densities measured by direct scan at the currently chosen star, so the trichotomy and its characteristic dips at composite charges become visible at a glance.",
      "html": "<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">

<style>

  *{box-sizing:border-box}

<body>
<div class="wrap">
  <h1>Charge, Resolution and Brightness Laboratory</h1>
  <p class="sub">
    Fix a boundary rational p/q and a charge k. The ray of charge k at p/q is the straight line
    Re z = p/q + (k/q)·Im z, a curve at constant hyperbolic distance arsinh(|k|/q) from the
    geodesic over p/q. Which lattice points on it are genuine Pythagorean seeds? Choose Bézout
    integers x, y with qx − py = 1; then the points of the ray are exactly
    (m, n) = (qA + yk, pA + xk) for A ∈ ℤ, and the two seed conditions collapse to
    gcd(A, k) = 1 plus at most one parity class. This laboratory scans the lattice directly and
    compares the count with the predicted totient law.
  </p>

  <div class="grid">
    <div class="panel">
      <h2>Parameters</h2>
      <label>numerator p = <b id="pO">1</b></label>
      <input type="range" id="p" min="0" max="15" value="1"/>
      <label>denominator q = <b id="qO">3</b></label>
      <input type="range" id="q" min="1" max="15" value="3"/>
      <label>charge k = <b id="kO">3</b></label>
      <input type="range" id="k" min="1" max="30" value="3"/>
      <label>window offset a = <b id="aO">0</b></label>
      <input type="range" id="a" min="0" max="40" value="0"/>

      <h2 style="margin-top:16px">Star data</h2>
      <div id="stardata"></div>
    </div>

    <div>
      <div class="panel">
        <h2>The census: predicted versus scanned</h2>
        <div id="verdict" class="verdict"></div>
        <table id="tbl"></table>
      </div>
      <div class="panel" style="margin-top:16px">
        <h2>Density along the ray, as a function of the charge</h2>
        <canvas id="cv" width="1180" height="330"></canvas>
        <p style="color:var(--dim);font-size:12.5px;line-height:1.55;margin:10px 0 0">
          Green: φ(k)/k, the density in the two full-brightness regimes (both p and q odd, or
          the charge even). Orange: φ(k)/(2k), the half-brightness of the mixed regime
          (p + q odd and k odd). Crosses: the density measured by direct lattice scan at the
          currently selected star. The dips are the highly composite charges — a ray of charge
          105 = 3·5·7 keeps only (2/3)(4/5)(6/7) ≈ 45.7% of its lattice points.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>

<script>
function gcd(a,b){a=Math.abs(a);b=Math.abs(b);while(b){[a,b]=[b,a%b];}return a;}
function totient(k){let r=k,x=k;for(let d=2;d*d<=x;d++){if(x%d===0){while(x%d===0)x/=d;r-=r/d;}}if(x>1)r-=r/x;return Math.round(r);}
function bez(p,q){ // x,y with q x - p y = 1
  let oldR=q,r=p,oldA=1,a=0,oldB=0,b=1;
  while(r!==0){const t=Math.floor(oldR/r);
    [oldR,r]=[r,oldR-t*r];[oldA,a]=[a,oldA-t*a];[oldB,b]=[b,oldB-t*b];}
  return [oldA,-oldB]; // q*oldA + p*oldB = 1  =>  q*x - p*y = 1 with y = -oldB
}
function starGap(p,q){return ((p+q)%2===1)?1:2;}
function isSeedPair(m,n){return gcd(m,n)===1 && (((m%2)+(n%2))%2===1);}

function measuredDensity(p,q,k){
  const [x,y]=bez(p,q);let hits=0;
  for(let A=0;A<2*k;A++){
    const m=q*A+y*k, n=p*A+x*k;
    if(gcd(m,n)===1 && Math.abs((m+n))%2===1) hits++;
  }
  return hits/(2*k);
}

function refresh(){
  let p=+document.getElementById('p').value;
  let q=+document.getElementById('q').value;
  const k=+document.getElementById('k').value;
  const a=+document.getElementById('a').value;
  if(q<1)q=1; if(p>q)p=q;
  const g=gcd(p,q);
  if(g>1){p/=g;q/=g;}
  document.getElementById('pO').textContent=p;
  document.getElementById('qO').textContent=q;
  document.getElementById('kO').textContent=k;
  document.getElementById('aO').textContent=a;

  const [x,y]=bez(p,q), gap=starGap(p,q), bothOdd=(p%2===1&&q%2===1);
  const admissible = (!bothOdd) || (k%2===1);
  const regime = bothOdd ? 'both odd → full brightness'
               : (k%2===0 ? 'p+q odd, k even → full brightness'
                          : 'p+q odd, k odd → half brightness');
  const predicted = (bothOdd || k%2===0) ? 2*totient(k) : totient(k);

  // direct scan of the window
  let rows='<tr><th class="l">ray parameter A</th><th>m = qA+yk</th><th>n = pA+xk</th>'
          +'<th>gcd(m,n)</th><th>m+n</th><th>seed?</th></tr>';
  let counted=0;
  for(let A=a;A<a+2*k;A++){
    const m=q*A+y*k, n=p*A+x*k, gg=gcd(m,n), par=((m+n)%2+2)%2;
    const ok = (gg===1 && par===1);
    if(ok)counted++;
    if(2*k<=24||A-a<12)
      rows+=`<tr><td class="l">${A}</td><td>${m}</td><td>${n}</td><td>${gg}</td>`
           +`<td>${par===1?'odd':'even'}</td><td class="${ok?'ok':'bad'}">${ok?'yes':'—'}</td></tr>`;
  }
  if(2*k>24) rows+=`<tr><td class="l" colspan="6" style="color:#93a0c0">… ${2*k-12} further`
                  +` parameters scanned but not listed …</td></tr>`;
  document.getElementById('tbl').innerHTML=rows;

  document.getElementById('verdict').innerHTML =
    (!admissible
      ? `<b style="color:#f72585">Charge k = ${k} is not realised at ${p}/${q}.</b>
         Both p and q are odd, so every charge qn − pm is forced odd — this ray of the pencil is
         completely empty, and the scan below confirms it.<br/>`
      : ``) +
    `Regime: <code>${regime}</code>. Predicted census over a window of 2k = ${2*k} ray
     parameters: <code>${predicted}</code> = <code>${(bothOdd||k%2===0)?'2φ':'φ'}(${k})</code>
     with φ(${k}) = ${totient(k)}. Scanned: <code>${counted}</code>. ` +
    (counted===(admissible?predicted:0)

  "interactive_layout": "# The Pythagorean Star Map

### A guided tour of the fans that appear when right triangles are drawn in hyperbolic space

---

## 0. The one-minute version

Take every right triangle with whole-number sides. Plot each one as a single dot in the
hyperbolic plane, using a recipe so simple it looks like it could not possibly encode anything.
What comes out is not a cloud. It is a **star map**: sharp fans of straight lines shooting out
of certain points on the horizon, nothing at all at the points in between, and one lone bright
ray marching off into the interior.

By the end of this page you will know exactly which points grow fans (the rational ones, and
only those), how wide apart the rays of a fan are (a parity law), how densely populated each
ray is (Euler's totient function), and why the whole beautiful structure is completely useless
for breaking cryptography (a volume-growth argument).

{{visualization:0}}

Look at the yellow dots — those are the triangles. Everything else is the explanation.

---

## 1. Where the dots come from

Since Euclid we have known how to make every primitive Pythagorean triple. Choose two whole
numbers $m > n > 0$ that are coprime and of opposite parity — call such a pair a **seed** — and
set

$$a = m^2 - n^2, \qquad b = 2mn, \qquad c = m^2 + n^2 .$$

Then $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$, and every primitive triple arises from exactly one seed. The seed
$(2,1)$ gives $(3,4,5)$; $(3,2)$ gives $(5,12,13)$; $(4,1)$ gives $(15,8,17)$.

In 1934 B. Berggren noticed that the triples form a **tree**. Three moves,

$$B_1(m,n) = (2m-n,\ m), \qquad B_2(m,n) = (2m+n,\ m), \qquad B_3(m,n) = (m+2n,\ n),$$

generate every seed from the root $(2,1)$, each one exactly once. And the plot above is what you
get by sending each seed to the point

$$z(m,n) \;=\; \frac{n+i}{m} \;=\; \underbrace{\frac nm}_{\text{horizontal}} \;+\; \underbrace{\frac im}_{\text{height}} .$$

<details>
<summary><b>Why the upper half-plane is not just graph paper</b> — click for the hyperbolic background</summary>

The set $\mathbb{H} = \{z : \operatorname{Im} z > 0\}$ with the length element
$ds = |dz|/\operatorname{Im} z$ is the standard model of the
[hyperbolic plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poincar%C3%A9_half-plane_model). Distances
satisfy

$$\cosh d(z,w) = 1 + \frac{|z-w|^2}{2\operatorname{Im}z\,\operatorname{Im}w},$$

geodesics are vertical half-lines and semicircles meeting the real axis at right angles, and the
real axis itself is infinitely far away: it is the *ideal boundary*.

The first surprise is what this metric reads off our plot. A short computation gives the
**radial law**

$$\cosh d\big(i,\ z(m,n)\big) \;=\; \frac{m^2+n^2+1}{2m} \;=\; \frac{c+1}{2m},$$

so the hypotenuse $c$ of the triple appears even though the plot only used the ratios $n/m$ and
$1/m$. Squeezing the formula gives
$\tfrac12\log c \le d \le \tfrac12\log(2(c+1))$: each triple sits at hyperbolic radius
$\tfrac12\log c$, to within $\log 2$. The tree grows outward exactly as fast as its hypotenuses
grow.
</details>

---

## 2. Charges: the invariant that draws the lines

Fix a rational point $p/q$ on the horizon, in lowest terms. Every node lies on exactly one
straight Euclidean line through it, and which line is determined by a single integer:

$$\operatorname{Re} z \;=\; \frac pq \;+\; \frac kq \operatorname{Im} z, \qquad
\boxed{\ k \;=\; qn - pm\ }$$

This $k$ is the **star charge** of the node at $p/q$. The fans in the picture are its level
sets. Better still, the charge has a purely geometric meaning: the line of charge $k$ is a
**hypercycle**, the set of points at constant hyperbolic distance

$$d\big(z,\ \gamma_{p/q}\big) \;=\; \operatorname{arsinh}\frac{|k|}{q}$$

from the vertical geodesic $\gamma_{p/q}$ rising out of $p/q$. So the charge is literally the
width of the ray, measured hyperbolically.

Play with it. Choose a boundary rational in the explorer below and watch the fan light up;
the readout tells you which charges are allowed, how far apart the rays are, and whether the
fan is one of the six you can actually see.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

<details>
<summary><b>Why a ray looks like a continuous line rather than scattered dots</b></summary>

Two facts. First, the nodes on a ray are the lattice translates $(m+tq,\ n+tp)$ of one another,
and the exact distance between two of them is

$$\cosh d\big(z(m,n),\ z(m+tq,\,n+tp)\big) = \frac{(tk)^2 + m^2 + (m+tq)^2}{2m(m+tq)} .$$

Consecutive nodes therefore satisfy $\cosh(\text{step}) = 1 + O(1/j^2)$ as you walk out along
the ray: **the steps shrink to zero**. Second, the ray converges to its own tip: both
$\operatorname{Im} z_j$ and $|\operatorname{Re} z_j - p/q|$ are $O(1/j)$.

An infinite path of shrinking steps gliding into a boundary point is exactly what the eye reads
as a smooth straight line.
</details>

---

## 3. The parity law: why $0.2$ has a fan and $0.25$ does not

Here is the first genuinely arithmetic phenomenon. Suppose $p$ and $q$ are **both odd**. Since
every seed has $m+n$ odd, working modulo $2$ gives

$$k = qn - pm \equiv n + m \equiv 1 \pmod 2 .$$

**Every charge is odd.** Half of the pencil is empty and the surviving rays sit twice as far
apart. When $p+q$ is odd instead, no such obstruction exists, and in fact every integer charge
occurs — infinitely often, and one can write down the seeds explicitly.

{{algorithm:0}}

This gives the complete **spectrum**: at $p/q$, an integer $k$ is a charge if and only if $p+q$
is odd or $k$ is odd. It also determines the **resolution** of the fan, the minimum separation
between two populated rays measured in $\sinh$ of their widths:

$$\delta(p/q) \;=\;
\begin{cases} 1/q, & p+q \text{ odd},\\[2pt] 2/q, & p,q \text{ both odd}.\end{cases}$$

Rank the rationals of $[0,1]$ by $\delta$ and ask which ones clear the bar $2/5$. The answer is
a finite list:

$$0, \qquad \tfrac15, \qquad \tfrac13, \qquad \tfrac12, \qquad \tfrac35, \qquad 1 .$$

Those are exactly the fans in the picture — $0$, $0.2$, $0.333$, $0.5$, $0.6$, $1$ — and note who
is missing: $1/4 = 0.25$, whose denominator is *smaller* than $5$ but whose coordinate sum is
odd, so it forfeits the factor-two bonus. The parity law is what decides between $0.2$ and
$0.25$.

{{algorithm:2}}

{{visualization:1}}

<details>
<summary><b>The hierarchy is finite at every scale</b></summary>

Because the parity factor is at most $2$, the condition $\delta(p/q) \ge \varepsilon$ forces
$q \le 2/\varepsilon$. So for any threshold only finitely many fans qualify: zoom into the
picture and new fans appear, always finitely many at a time, forever. There is no scale at
which the star map dissolves into a continuum of fans.
</details>

---

## 4. Brightness: Euler's totient counts the dots

Resolution tells you how far apart the rays of a fan are. **Brightness** tells you how densely
one ray is populated — and this is where a classical arithmetic function appears.

The trick is a change of coordinates. Pick integers $x, y$ with $qx - py = 1$ (extended
Euclid). Then the integer points of the ray of charge $k$ are exactly

$$(m,n) \;=\; (qA + yk,\ pA + xk), \qquad A \in \mathbb{Z},$$

and in this coordinate the coprimality condition for a seed becomes stunningly simple:

$$\gcd(m,n) = 1 \iff \gcd(A,k) = 1 .$$

**The charge is the only arithmetic obstruction along a ray.** On the unit rays $k = \pm1$ there
is no obstruction at all: every lattice point is a genuine triple, and those are the brightest
lines in every fan.

Counting the rest is a residue count, and it produces a clean trichotomy. In a window of $2k$
consecutive ray parameters, the number of Pythagorean nodes is

| regime | count per window of $2k$ |
|---|---|
| $p,q$ both odd (so $k$ odd) | $2\varphi(k)$ |
| $p+q$ odd, $k$ even | $2\varphi(k)$ |
| $p+q$ odd, $k$ odd | $\varphi(k) = \varphi(2k)$ — half brightness |

where $\varphi$ is [Euler's totient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler%27s_totient_function).
So a ray of prime charge $r$ has density $1-1/r$, and a ray of charge $105 = 3\cdot5\cdot7$
keeps only $\tfrac23\cdot\tfrac45\cdot\tfrac67 \approx 45.7\%$ of its lattice points and looks
visibly dotted.

Test the law yourself — the laboratory below scans the lattice directly and compares:

{{interactive_demo:1}}

{{algorithm:1}}

<details>
<summary><b>Conservation of light</b> — the hidden symmetry between the two laws</summary>

Notice the compensation. At a both-odd rational the rays are spaced $2/q$ apart, twice as far
as elsewhere — but each is twice as bright, $2\varphi(k)$ per window. At a mixed-parity rational
the rays are twice as finely spaced and each carries half as many nodes. The total amount of
"light" near the boundary point is the same; parity only decides how it is divided between
angular resolution and per-ray intensity.
</details>

---

## 5. Nothing at the irrationals

Why are there no fans between the rationals, given how densely the dots crowd the boundary?
Because of a three-line argument that admits no exceptions.

> **No star at an irrational point.** If two nodes $z(m,n)$ and $z(m',n')$ lie on a single
> straight line through an irrational boundary point $\alpha$, then they are the same node.

Indeed the two hypotheses read $n = \alpha m + c$ and $n' = \alpha m' + c$; subtracting,
$\alpha(m-m') = n-n'$. If $m \ne m'$ this makes $\alpha$ a ratio of integers. So $m = m'$, and
then $n = n'$.

A fan needs two nodes collinear with its tip. Collinearity with an irrational tip is impossible.
**Straightness is a rational phenomenon** — and this is despite the nodes accumulating at *every*
point of $[0,1]$, irrational ones included.

<details>
<summary><b>The three moves, and the one that is different</b></summary>

On slopes $t = n/m$, the tree's moves act as
$B_1 : t \mapsto \frac1{2-t}$, $B_2 : t \mapsto \frac1{2+t}$, $B_3 : t \mapsto \frac t{1+2t}$,
with disjoint images $(\tfrac12,1)$, $(\tfrac13,\tfrac12)$, $(0,\tfrac13)$ — a trichotomy that
also inverts the tree and reproves Berggren's theorem.

The outer two are [parabolic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%B6bius_transformation): in the
right coordinate they are simply $x \mapsto x+1$ and $x \mapsto x+2$, they fix the *rational*
points $1$ and $0$, and their orbits crawl in at rate $\Theta(1/k)$. They preserve $m-n$ and $n$
respectively, which are precisely the charges at $1$ and $0$: **the fans at $0$ and $1$ are the
orbits of the two parabolic moves.**

The middle move $B_2$ is hyperbolic. It contracts by a factor of $4$ toward the *irrational*
fixed point $\sqrt2-1$, its orbit from the root runs through the
[Pell numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pell_number) $(2,1),(5,2),(12,5),(29,12),\dots$,
and the ratios converge to the [silver ratio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_ratio)
$1+\sqrt2$. Its steps do **not** shrink — they converge to $\log(1+\sqrt2) = 0.881373\ldots$,
the translation length of a hyperbolic isometry. That is the lone bright diagonal ray in the
picture, and by the no-star theorem its irrational tip can never grow a fan.
</details>

---

## 6. The cryptographic dead end

Why would anyone plot Pythagorean triples in hyperbolic space at all? Because of a temptation.
A number with two different representations as a sum of two squares can be **factored**, by a
trick Euler already knew: if $N = m_1^2+n_1^2 = m_2^2+n_2^2$ then with $P = m_1m_2+n_1n_2$,

$$\gcd(N,P)\cdot \gcd(N,\ m_1n_2+n_1m_2) \;=\; N,$$

both factors non-trivial. For $N = 65 = 8^2+1^2 = 7^2+4^2$: $P=60$, $\gcd(65,60)=5$, and the
partner is $13$.

Two such representations are two nodes with the same hypotenuse — a **collision** — and both sit
at radius $\tfrac12\log N + O(1)$. Could a short hyperbolic walk find one from the other?

{{algorithm:4}}

No, and twice over.

**The divisor pushes the witnesses apart.** An exact computation using the
Brahmagupta–Fibonacci identity gives $\cosh d(z_1,z_2) \ge 1 + g/2$ where $g = \gcd(N,P)$ is the
divisor the method extracts, hence

$$d(z_1,z_2) \;\ge\; \log g - \log 2 .$$

The more useful the collision, the further apart its two witnesses; for a balanced factorisation
they are essentially antipodal on their circle.

**And the ball is already full.** A node lies within distance $R$ of $i$ exactly when
$(m - \cosh R)^2 + n^2 \le \sinh^2 R$ — a transcendental condition that collapses into an
ordinary Euclidean disc — and counting lattice points shows the ball contains $\Theta(e^{2R})$
nodes, matching hyperbolic *area*. The smallest ball guaranteed to contain the collision for $N$
has radius $\approx \tfrac12\log N + \log 2$, so it contains $\Theta(N)$ nodes.

{{algorithm:3}}

The hyperbolic metric compresses the search space and the search target by the same exponential
factor. The geodesic to the answer is short; the number of places the answer might be is linear
in $N$. Trial enumeration in $O(\sqrt N)$ stays ahead.

{{demo:1}}

---

## 8. What is still open

- **Vanishing width at irrationals.** Is
  $\inf\{d(z(m,n),\gamma_\alpha)\} = 0$ for every irrational $\alpha$, even though no
  positive-width line over $\alpha$ carries two nodes? Continued fractions should do it: a seed
  near $\gamma_\alpha$ is a convergent $p_j/q_j$ of the right parity, and among two consecutive
  convergents at least one has $p_j+q_j$ odd, because $p_{j+1}q_j - p_jq_{j+1} = \pm1$ forbids
  both from being even-even.
- **The exact star count.** Numerically the ball of radius $R$ holds
  $0.13024\,e^{2R}$ nodes; the predicted constant is
  $\frac{\pi+2}{4\pi^2} = 0.13023806\ldots$, from the seed-cone area $\frac\pi4+\frac12$ and the
  seed density $4/\pi^2$. Proving it is a Gauss circle problem with a parity sieve.
- **Step statistics of an arbitrary path.** Along the fans the steps tend to $0$, along the
  spine to $\log(1+\sqrt2)$. Do the Cesàro averages converge for *every* infinite word in the
  three moves, and is the set of limits exactly $[0, \log(1+\sqrt2)]$?
- **A modular home.** The three moves generate a subgroup of $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$;
  identifying the congruence subgroup should turn the parity asymmetry into a cusp width and
  might give equidistribution of the nodes on each annulus for free.

---

### The takeaway

Somebody plotted an ancient theorem in a curved space and saw lines that had no business being
there. Every one of those lines turned out to be a theorem: a parity law decides which fans you
see, a totient decides how bright they are, an irrationality argument decides that there is
nothing in between, and a volume count decides that none of it will help you factor a number.
The picture was not an illustration of the mathematics. The picture *was* the mathematics, drawn
at a resolution the eye happens to be good at.

/-!
# The individual rays of a rational star: straight lines, shrinking steps, ideal tips

`Cryptography.BerggrenStars.RationalStars` determines *which* rays of the pencil over a
boundary rational `p/q` are populated by Berggren nodes. This file studies a single ray.

Fix a boundary rational `p/q` and a star charge `k = q n - p m`. The nodes of charge `k` are
exactly the lattice translates `(m + t q, n + t p)` of one another, and here we prove that they
form the visible radial line of the picture:

* `star_ray_line` : the exact Euclidean equation of the ray,

* `ray_constant_distVLine` : two nodes of equal charge are at equal hyperbolic distance from

* `cross_along_ray` : the seed cross product of two nodes on a ray of charge `k` at lattice

/-! ## Part 1. The ray is a Euclidean straight line through `p/q`, and a hypercycle -/

/-- **The equation of the radial line.** Every node lies on the Euclidean line through the
ideal point `p/q` with parameter `charge / q`. Nodes of equal charge are exactly collinear
along such a line: this is the radial line seen in the picture. -/
theorem star_ray_line (p q m n : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hq : 0 < q) :
    (hpoint m n hm).re
      = (p : ℝ) / q + ((starCharge p q m n : ℝ) / q) * (hpoint m n hm).im := by
  have hM : (0 : ℝ) < (m : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hm
  have hQ : (0 : ℝ) < (q : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hq
  rw [hpoint_re, hpoint_im, starCharge]
  push_cast
  field_simp
  ring

/-- **A ray is a hypercycle.** Nodes with the same charge at `p/q` are at the same hyperbolic
distance from the vertical geodesic over `p/q`. -/
theorem ray_constant_distVLine (p q m n m' n' : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hm' : 0 < m') (hq : 0 < q)
    (h : starCharge p q m n = starCharge p q m' n') :
    distVLine (hpoint m n hm) ((p : ℝ) / q) = distVLine (hpoint m' n' hm') ((p : ℝ) / q) := by
  have h1 := sinh_distVLine_charge p q m n hm hq
  have h2 := sinh_distVLine_charge p q m' n' hm' hq
  have : Real.sinh (distVLine (hpoint m n hm) ((p : ℝ) / q))
      = Real.sinh (distVLine (hpoint m' n' hm') ((p : ℝ) / q)) := by
    rw [h1, h2, h]
  exact Real.sinh_injective this

/-! ## Part 2. The arithmetic of a ray: the unit rays are fully populated -/

/-- Any common divisor of the coordinates of a node divides its star charge. Hence on the rays
of charge `±1` **all** lattice points are primitive. -/
theorem dvd_charge_of_common_divisor (p q m n : ℕ) {d : ℕ} (h1 : d ∣ m) (h2 : d ∣ n) :
    (d : ℤ) ∣ starCharge p q m n := by
  obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := h1
  obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := h2
  refine ⟨(q : ℤ) * b - (p : ℤ) * a, ?_⟩
  simp only [starCharge]
  push_cast
  ring

  · -- coprimality: a common divisor divides the charge `±1`
    have hd : (Nat.gcd (m + 2 * t * q) (n + 2 * t * p) : ℤ)
        ∣ starCharge p q (m + 2 * t * q) (n + 2 * t * p) :=

  rw [hcross]

/-! ## Part 0. The star charge -/

/-- The **star charge** of the node `z(m,n)` at the boundary rational `p/q`:
`k = q n - p m`. The node lies on the Euclidean ray out of `p/q` of parameter `k/q`. -/
def starCharge (p q m n : ℕ) : ℤ := (q : ℤ) * n - (p : ℤ) * m

/-- Charges are constant along the lattice line: translating a node by the primitive vector
`(q,p)` keeps it on the same ray of the star at `p/q`. -/
theorem starCharge_translate (p q m n t : ℕ) :
    starCharge p q (m + t * q) (n + t * p) = starCharge p q m n := by
  simp only [starCharge]; push_cast; ring

/-! ## Part 1. Quantisation: the parity obstruction -/

/-- Parity as a statement in `ZMod 2`. -/
theorem odd_iff_cast_zmod_two (z : ℤ) : Odd z ↔ ((z : ZMod 2) = 1) := by
  rw [Int.odd_iff, show ((1 : ZMod 2)) = ((1 : ℤ) : ZMod 2) by norm_num,
    ZMod.intCast_eq_intCast_iff']
  norm_num

/-- **Quantisation of a both-odd star.** If `p` and `q` are both odd, the charge of any Euclid
seed at `p/q` is odd: only every second ray of the pencil is populated. -/
theorem charge_odd_of_odd_odd {p q m n : ℕ} (hp : p % 2 = 1) (hq : q % 2 = 1)
    (h : IsSeed m n) : Odd (starCharge p q m n) := by
  have hp2 : ((p : ℤ) : ZMod 2) = 1 :=
    (odd_iff_cast_zmod_two _).mp (by rw [Int.odd_iff]; omega)
  have hq2 : ((q : ℤ) : ZMod 2) = 1 :=
    (odd_iff_cast_zmod_two _).mp (by rw [Int.odd_iff]; omega)
  have hmn : ((m : ℤ) : ZMod 2) + ((n : ℤ) : ZMod 2) = 1 := by
    have hodd : Odd ((m : ℤ) + n) := by
      have := h.parity; rw [Int.odd_iff]; omega
    have h2 := (odd_iff_cast_zmod_two _).mp hodd
    rw [Int.cast_add] at h2
    exact h2
  rw [odd_iff_cast_zmod_two]

      = ((q : ℤ) : ZMod 2) * ((n : ℤ) : ZMod 2) - ((p : ℤ) : ZMod 2) * ((m : ℤ) : ZMod 2) := by
    simp [starCharge]
  rw [hcast, hp2, hq2]
  have key : ∀ a b : ZMod 2, a + b = 1 → (1 : ZMod 2) * b - 1 * a = 1 := by decide
  exact key _ _ hmn

/-! ## Part 2. Realisation: the `SL₂(ℤ)` ray construction -/

/-- The determinant-one change of variables. If `q x - p y = 1` then the map
`(A,k) ↦ (qA + yk, pA + xk)` is in `SL₂(ℤ)`, so it preserves coprimality: the node built from
`(A,k)` is primitive as soon as `A` and `k` are. -/
theorem isCoprime_of_sl2_charge {p q x y A k : ℤ} (hdet : q * x - p * y = 1)
    (h : IsCoprime A k) : IsCoprime (q * A + y * k) (p * A + x * k) := by
  obtain ⟨u, v, huv⟩ := h
  refine ⟨u * x - v * p, v * q - u * y, ?_⟩
  have hA : x * (q * A + y * k) - y * (p * A + x * k) = A * (q * x - p * y) := by ring
  have hk : q * (p * A + x * k) - p * (q * A + y * k) = k * (q * x - p * y) := by ring
  rw [hdet, mul_one] at hA hk
  calc (u * x - v * p) * (q * A + y * k) + (v * q - u * y) * (p * A + x * k)
      = u * (x * (q * A + y * k) - y * (p * A + x * k))
        + v * (q * (p * A + x * k) - p * (q * A + y * k)) := by ring
    _ = u * A + v * k := by rw [hA, hk]
    _ = 1 := huv

/-- The parity bookkeeping of the construction, as an identity in `ZMod 2`. -/
theorem parity_zmod_two (P Q X Y K A : ZMod 2) (hdet : Q * X - P * Y = 1)
    (hA : A = 1 + K * (X + Y)) (hpar : P + Q = 1 ∨ K = 1) :
    (P + Q) * A + (X + Y) * K = 1 := by
  revert hdet hA hpar
  revert P Q X Y K A
  decide

/-! ## Part 3. The exact charge spectrum of a rational star -/

/-- The central ray `k = 0` of the star at `p/q` — the vertical geodesic itself — carries a
Berggren node if and only if the pair `(q,p)` is a Euclid seed, and then that node is unique. -/
theorem charge_zero_iff {p q m n : ℕ} (hp : 0 < p) (hlt : p < q) (hcop : Nat.Coprime p q)
    (h : IsSeed m n) : starCharge p q m n = 0 ↔ (m = q ∧ n = p) := by
  constructor
  · intro h0
    have hqn : q * n = p * m := by
      have : (q : ℤ) * n = (p : ℤ) * m := by
        have := h0; rw [starCharge] at this; linarith
      exact_mod_cast this
    have hqm : q ∣ m := by
      have : q ∣ p * m := ⟨n, hqn.symm⟩
      exact (Nat.Coprime.dvd_of_dvd_mul_left (Nat.coprime_comm.mp hcop) this)
    have hmq : m ∣ q := by
      have : m ∣ q * n := ⟨p, by rw [hqn, Nat.mul_comm]⟩
      exact (Nat.Coprime.dvd_of_dvd_mul_right h.cop this)
    have hmq' : m = q := Nat.dvd_antisymm hmq hqm
    subst hmq'
    have : m * n = p * m := by omega
    have hm0 : 0 < m := lt_trans h.pos h.lt
    exact ⟨rfl, by nlinarith⟩
  · rintro ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    simp [starCharge]
    ring

/-- **The charge spectrum of a rational star.** For `0 < p < q` coprime, an integer `k` is the
star charge of some Berggren node at the boundary point `p/q` **iff** `p + q` is odd or `k` is
odd. So: a star at a rational with `p+q` odd is *fully* populated (every ray of the pencil
carries infinitely many nodes), whereas a star with `p, q` both odd has only its odd rays. -/
theorem star_spectrum (p q : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) (hlt : p < q) (hcop : Nat.Coprime p q) (k : ℤ) :
    (∃ m n : ℕ, IsSeed m n ∧ starCharge p q m n = k) ↔ ((p + q) % 2 = 1 ∨ Odd k) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨m, n, hseed, rfl⟩
    rcases Nat.even_or_odd (p + q) with he | ho
    · right
      have hp2 : p % 2 = 1 := by
        rcases Nat.even_or_odd p with hpe | hpo
        · exfalso
          have hq2 : q % 2 = 0 := by
            rw [Nat.even_iff] at he hpe; omega
          have hp2 : p % 2 = 0 := by rw [Nat.even_iff] at hpe; omega
          have : 2 ∣ Nat.gcd p q := Nat.dvd_gcd (by omega) (by omega)
          rw [hcop] at this
          omega
        · rw [Nat.odd_iff] at hpo; exact hpo
      have hq2 : q % 2 = 1 := by rw [Nat.even_iff] at he; omega
      exact charge_odd_of_odd_odd hp2 hq2 hseed
    · left; rw [Nat.odd_iff] at ho; exact ho
  · intro hk
    by_cases hk0 : k = 0
    · subst hk0
      have hpar : (p + q) % 2 = 1 := by
        rcases hk with h | h
        · exact h
        · exact absurd h (by simp)
      refine ⟨q, p, ⟨hp, hlt, Nat.coprime_comm.mp hcop, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
      simp [starCharge]
      ring
    · obtain ⟨m, n, hs, _, hc⟩ := exists_seed_of_charge p q hp hlt hcop k hk0 hk 0
      exact ⟨m, n, hs, hc⟩

/-! ## Part 4. The resolution law and the visible rationals -/

/-- The numerator of the **angular resolution** of the star at `p/q`: adjacent populated rays
of the pencil differ by `starGapNum p q / q` in `sinh` of the distance to the central
geodesic. -/
def starGapNum (p q : ℕ) : ℕ := if (p + q) % 2 = 1 then 1 else 2

/-- The hyperbolic sine of the distance from a node to the geodesic over `p/q` is exactly
`|charge| / q`: the star charge *is* the (scaled) hypercycle radius. -/
theorem sinh_distVLine_charge (p q m n : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hq : 0 < q) :
    Real.sinh (distVLine (hpoint m n hm) ((p : ℝ) / q))
      = |(starCharge p q m n : ℝ)| / q := by
  have hM : (0 : ℝ) < (m : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hm
  have hQ : (0 : ℝ) < (q : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hq
  rw [sinh_distVLine, hpoint_re, hpoint_im, starCharge]
  push_cast
  rw [show (n : ℝ) / m - (p : ℝ) / q = ((q : ℝ) * n - (p : ℝ) * m) / ((q : ℝ) * m) by
      field_simp,
    abs_div, abs_of_pos (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) < (q : ℝ) * m)]
  field_simp

/-- **Resolution law (lower bound).** Two Berggren nodes lying on *different* rays of the star
at `p/q` are separated, in `sinh` of their distances to the central geodesic, by at least
`starGapNum p q / q`. For `p, q` both odd this is twice as large as otherwise: the parity
obstruction doubles the resolution of the star. -/
theorem charge_gap {p q m₁ n₁ m₂ n₂ : ℕ} (hp : p % 2 = 1 ∨ q % 2 = 1) (hq : 0 < q)
    (hm₁ : 0 < m₁) (hm₂ : 0 < m₂) (h₁ : IsSeed m₁ n₁) (h₂ : IsSeed m₂ n₂)
    (hne : |starCharge p q m₁ n₁| ≠ |starCharge p q m₂ n₂|) :
    (starGapNum p q : ℝ) / q ≤
      |Real.sinh (distVLine (hpoint m₁ n₁ hm₁) ((p : ℝ) / q))
        - Real.sinh (distVLine (hpoint m₂ n₂ hm₂) ((p : ℝ) / q))| := by
  have hQ : (0 : ℝ) < q := by exact_mod_cast hq
  set k₁ := starCharge p q m₁ n₁ with hk₁
  set k₂ := starCharge p q m₂ n₂ with hk₂
  have hsub : |k₁| - |k₂| ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr hne
  have hgap : (starGapNum p q : ℤ) ≤ |(|k₁| - |k₂|)| := by
    unfold starGapNum
    split_ifs with hpar
    · simpa using Int.one_le_abs hsub
    · -- both `p` and `q` are odd, so both charges are odd and `||k₁| - |k₂||` is even and ≠ 0
      have hp2 : p % 2 = 1 := by
        rcases hp with h | h
        · exact h
        · omega
      have hq2 : q % 2 = 1 := by omega
      have o₁ : Odd k₁ := charge_odd_of_odd_odd hp2 hq2 h₁
      have o₂ : Odd k₂ := charge_odd_of_odd_odd hp2 hq2 h₂
      rw [Int.odd_iff] at o₁ o₂
      have a₁ : |k₁| % 2 = 1 := by rcases abs_choice k₁ with h | h <;> omega
      have a₂ : |k₂| % 2 = 1 := by rcases abs_choice k₂ with h | h <;> omega
      have hdvd : (2 : ℤ) ∣ |(|k₁| - |k₂|)| := by
        have : (2 : ℤ) ∣ (|k₁| - |k₂|) := by omega
        exact (dvd_abs _ _).mpr this
      exact Int.le_of_dvd (abs_pos.mpr hsub) hdvd
  have hcast : |(|(k₁ : ℝ)| - |(k₂ : ℝ)|)| = ((|(|k₁| - |k₂|)| : ℤ) : ℝ) := by
    push_cast
    simp
  rw [sinh_distVLine_charge p q m₁ n₁ hm₁ hq, sinh_distVLine_charge p q m₂ n₂ hm₂ hq,
    ← sub_div, abs_div, abs_of_pos hQ, ← hk₁, ← hk₂, div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hQ]
  rw [hcast]
  exact_mod_cast hgap

/-- **Resolution law (sharpness).** The bound of `charge_gap` is attained: at every rational
`p/q` with `0 < p < q` there are two Berggren nodes whose distances to the central geodesic

theorem star_gap_attained (p q : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) (hlt : p < q) (hcop : Nat.Coprime p q) :
    ∃ (m₁ n₁ m₂ n₂ : ℕ) (h₁ : 0 < m₁) (h₂ : 0 < m₂), IsSeed m₁ n₁ ∧ IsSeed m₂ n₂ ∧
      |Real.sinh (distVLine (hpoint m₁ n₁ h₁) ((p : ℝ) / q))

  have hq : 0 < q := lt_trans hp hlt
  have hQ : (0 : ℝ) < q := by exact_mod_cast hq
  set g : ℕ := starGapNum p q with hg
  have hgpar : (p + q) % 2 = 1 ∨ Odd (1 + (g : ℤ)) := by
    unfold starGapNum at hg
    split_ifs at hg with hpar
    · left; exact hpar
    · right; rw [hg]; decide
  obtain ⟨m₁, n₁, hs₁, _, hc₁⟩ :=
    exists_seed_of_charge p q hp hlt hcop 1 (by norm_num) (by right; decide) 0
  obtain ⟨m₂, n₂, hs₂, _, hc₂⟩ :=
    exists_seed_of_charge p q hp hlt hcop (1 + (g : ℤ)) (by omega) hgpar 0
  have hm₁ : 0 < m₁ := lt_trans hs₁.pos hs₁.lt
  have hm₂ : 0 < m₂ := lt_trans hs₂.pos hs₂.lt
  refine ⟨m₁, n₁, m₂, n₂, hm₁, hm₂, hs₁, hs₂, ?_⟩
  have e1 : |(((1 : ℤ)) : ℝ)| = 1 := by norm_num
  have e2 : |(((1 + (g : ℤ)) : ℤ) : ℝ)| = 1 + (g : ℝ) := by
    rw [abs_of_nonneg (by push_cast; positivity)]
    push_cast
    ring
  rw [sinh_distVLine_charge p q m₁ n₁ hm₁ hq, sinh_distVLine_charge p q m₂ n₂ hm₂ hq,
    hc₁, hc₂, e1, e2, ← sub_div, abs_div, abs_of_pos hQ]
  congr 1
  rw [show (1 : ℝ) - (1 + (g : ℝ)) = -(g : ℝ) by ring, abs_neg,
    abs_of_nonneg (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (g : ℝ))]

/-- **The visible rationals.** Ranking the boundary rationals of `[0,1]` by the resolution
`δ(p/q) = starGapNum p q / q` of their star, the ones with `δ ≥ 2/5` are exactly

Berggren star map. Note that `1/4 = 0.25` is *absent* although `4 < 5`: an even denominator

both odd. -/
theorem visible_rationals (p q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (hle : p ≤ q) (hcop : Nat.Coprime p q) :

      (p = 0 ∧ q = 1) ∨ (p = 1 ∧ q = 1) ∨ (p = 1 ∧ q = 2) ∨ (p = 1 ∧ q = 3) ∨
        (p = 1 ∧ q = 5) ∨ (p = 3 ∧ q = 5) := by

  constructor
  · intro h
    have hq5 : q ≤ 5 := by split_ifs at h <;> omega
    interval_cases q <;> interval_cases p <;> simp_all [Nat.Coprime, Nat.gcd]

/-! ## Part 1. The `SL₂(ℤ)` parametrisation of a ray -/

/-- The **ray parameter** of an integer point, relative to Bezout data `q x - p y = 1`. -/
def rayParam (x y m n : ℤ) : ℤ := x * m - y * n

/-- **Parametrisation of a ray.** With `q x - p y = 1`, every integer point `(m,n)` is
recovered from its ray parameter `A = x m - y n` and its star charge `k = q n - p m` by
`(m,n) = (qA + yk, pA + xk)`. So the points of a fixed charge form a lattice line parametrised
by `A`, and the two Berggren conditions become conditions on `(A, k)`. -/
theorem ray_param_eq {p q : ℕ} {x y : ℤ} (hdet : (q : ℤ) * x - (p : ℤ) * y = 1) (m n : ℤ) :
    m = (q : ℤ) * rayParam x y m n + y * ((q : ℤ) * n - (p : ℤ) * m) ∧

  constructor
  · rw [rayParam]; linear_combination m * hdet.symm
  · rw [rayParam]; linear_combination n * hdet.symm

is coprime to the charge of the ray. Hence *the charge is the only arithmetic obstruction*: on
the rays of charge `±1` every lattice point is primitive. -/
theorem isCoprime_ray_iff {p q : ℕ} {x y : ℤ} (hdet : (q : ℤ) * x - (p : ℤ) * y = 1) (m n : ℤ) :
    IsCoprime m n ↔ IsCoprime (rayParam x y m n) ((q : ℤ) * n - (p : ℤ) * m) := by
  obtain ⟨hm, hn⟩ := ray_param_eq hdet m n
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨u, v, huv⟩
    refine ⟨u * q + v * p, u * y + v * x, ?_⟩
    calc (u * q + v * p) * rayParam x y m n
          + (u * y + v * x) * ((q : ℤ) * n - (p : ℤ) * m)
        = u * ((q : ℤ) * rayParam x y m n + y * ((q : ℤ) * n - (p : ℤ) * m))
          + v * ((p : ℤ) * rayParam x y m n + x * ((q : ℤ) * n - (p : ℤ) * m)) := by ring
      _ = u * m + v * n := by rw [← hm, ← hn]
      _ = 1 := huv
  · rintro ⟨u, v, huv⟩
    refine ⟨u * x - v * p, v * q - u * y, ?_⟩
    have hA : x * m - y * n = rayParam x y m n := rfl
    calc (u * x - v * p) * m + (v * q - u * y) * n
        = u * (x * m - y * n) + v * ((q : ℤ) * n - (p : ℤ) * m) := by ring
      _ = u * rayParam x y m n + v * ((q : ℤ) * n - (p : ℤ) * m) := by rw [hA]
      _ = 1 := huv

/-! ## Part 2. The two parity-free regimes -/

/-- With `p, q` both odd, the Bezout cofactors satisfy `x + y` odd.  This is the arithmetic
reason why the both-odd stars have their rays *doubly* spaced: `q x - p y = 1` forces
`x - y` odd. -/
theorem odd_bezout_sum {p q : ℕ} (hp : p % 2 = 1) (hq : q % 2 = 1) {x y : ℤ}
    (hdet : (q : ℤ) * x - (p : ℤ) * y = 1) : Odd (x + y) := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := Nat.odd_iff.mpr hp
  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := Nat.odd_iff.mpr hq
  have ha' : (p : ℤ) = 2 * a + 1 := by rw [ha]; push_cast; ring
  have hb' : (q : ℤ) = 2 * b + 1 := by rw [hb]; push_cast; ring
  rw [ha', hb'] at hdet
  exact ⟨-(b : ℤ) * x + (a : ℤ) * y + y, by linear_combination hdet⟩

/-- If `p` and `q` are both odd and the charge is odd, the parity condition along the ray holds
for *every* ray parameter: the only sieve on the ray is coprimality with the charge. -/
theorem parity_free_of_both_odd {p q : ℕ} (hp : p % 2 = 1) (hq : q % 2 = 1) {x y : ℤ}
    (hdet : (q : ℤ) * x - (p : ℤ) * y = 1) {k : ℤ} (hk : Odd k) (A : ℤ) :
    Odd (((p : ℤ) + q) * A + (x + y) * k) := by
  have hpq : Even ((p : ℤ) + q) := by
    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := Nat.odd_iff.mpr hp
    obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := Nat.odd_iff.mpr hq
    exact ⟨(a : ℤ) + b + 1, by rw [ha, hb]; push_cast; ring⟩
  exact (hpq.mul_right A).add_odd ((odd_bezout_sum hp hq hdet).mul hk)

/-- If the charge is even (and `p + q` is odd), coprimality with the charge already forces the
right parity: again the only sieve on the ray is coprimality. -/
theorem parity_free_of_even_charge {p q : ℕ} (hpq : (p + q) % 2 = 1) {x y : ℤ} {k : ℤ}
    (hk : Even k) {A : ℤ} (hA : IsCoprime A k) :
    Odd (((p : ℤ) + q) * A + (x + y) * k) := by
  -- `A` must be odd, since `gcd(A,k) = 1` and `k` is even
  have hAodd : Odd A := by
    rcases Int.even_or_odd A with hAe | hAo
    · exfalso
      obtain ⟨u, v, huv⟩ := hA
      obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := hAe
      obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := hk
      have h2 : (2 : ℤ) ∣ 1 := ⟨u * a + v * b, by linear_combination -huv⟩
      norm_num at h2
    · exact hAo
  have hpqodd : Odd ((p : ℤ) + q) := by
    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Nat.odd_iff.mpr hpq
    exact ⟨(c : ℤ), by have : ((p + q : ℕ) : ℤ) = 2 * c + 1 := by rw [hc]; push_cast; ring
                       push_cast at this; linarith⟩
  exact (hpqodd.mul hAodd).add_even (hk.mul_left (x + y))

/-! ## Part 3. The brightness law -/

/-- A window of `2k` consecutive integers contains exactly `2 φ(k)` integers coprime to `k`. -/
theorem window_coprime_card (k a : ℕ) :
    #{A ∈ Finset.Ico a (a + 2 * k) | Nat.Coprime k A} = 2 * Nat.totient k := by
  have hsplit : Finset.Ico a (a + 2 * k) = Finset.Ico a (a + k) ∪ Finset.Ico (a + k) (a + 2 * k) :=
    (Finset.Ico_union_Ico_eq_Ico (by omega) (by omega)).symm
  have hdisj : Disjoint (Finset.Ico a (a + k)) (Finset.Ico (a + k) (a + 2 * k)) :=
    Finset.Ico_disjoint_Ico_consecutive _ _ _
  rw [hsplit, Finset.filter_union, Finset.card_union_of_disjoint
    (Finset.disjoint_filter_filter hdisj)]
  have h1 : #{A ∈ Finset.Ico a (a + k) | Nat.Coprime k A} = Nat.totient k :=
    Nat.filter_coprime_Ico_eq_totient k a
  have h2 : #{A ∈ Finset.Ico (a + k) (a + 2 * k) | Nat.Coprime k A} = Nat.totient k := by
    have := Nat.filter_coprime_Ico_eq_totient k (a + k)
    rwa [show a + k + k = a + 2 * k by ring] at this
  rw [h1, h2]
  ring

/-- The arithmetic heart of the census: in ray coordinates the two Berggren conditions collapse
to the single condition `gcd(k, A) = 1`, in either parity-free regime. -/
theorem node_iff_coprime_of_both_odd {p q : ℕ} (hp : p % 2 = 1) (hq : q % 2 = 1) {x y : ℤ}
    (hdet : (q : ℤ) * x - (p : ℤ) * y = 1) {k : ℕ} (hk : k % 2 = 1) (A : ℕ) :
    (IsCoprime ((q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * k) ((p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * k) ∧
      Odd (((q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * k) + ((p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * k))) ↔ Nat.Coprime k A := by
  have hkodd : Odd (k : ℤ) := by rw [Int.odd_iff]; omega
  set m : ℤ := (q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * k with hm
  set n : ℤ := (p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * k with hn
  have hA : rayParam x y m n = (A : ℤ) := by
    simp only [rayParam, hm, hn]; linear_combination (A : ℤ) * hdet
  have hkk : (q : ℤ) * n - (p : ℤ) * m = (k : ℤ) := by
    simp only [hm, hn]; linear_combination (k : ℤ) * hdet
  have hsum : m + n = ((p : ℤ) + q) * (A : ℤ) + (x + y) * (k : ℤ) := by
    have h := sum_eq_ray hdet m n
    rwa [hA, hkk] at h
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hc, -⟩
    have hcop := (isCoprime_ray_iff hdet m n).mp hc
    rw [hA, hkk] at hcop
    have hg : Int.gcd (A : ℤ) (k : ℤ) = 1 := Int.isCoprime_iff_gcd_eq_one.mp hcop
    have hnat : Nat.Coprime A k := by simpa [Int.gcd_natCast_natCast] using hg
    exact hnat.symm
  · intro hc
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [isCoprime_ray_iff hdet, hA, hkk, Int.isCoprime_iff_gcd_eq_one]
      simpa [Int.gcd_natCast_natCast] using hc.symm
    · rw [hsum]
      exact parity_free_of_both_odd hp hq hdet hkodd (A : ℤ)

/-- Even-charge analogue of `node_iff_coprime_of_both_odd`. -/
theorem node_iff_coprime_of_even_charge {p q : ℕ} (hpq : (p + q) % 2 = 1) {x y : ℤ}
    (hdet : (q : ℤ) * x - (p : ℤ) * y = 1) {k : ℕ} (hk : k % 2 = 0) (A : ℕ) :
    (IsCoprime ((q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * k) ((p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * k) ∧
      Odd (((q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * k) + ((p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * k))) ↔ Nat.Coprime k A := by
  have hkeven : Even (k : ℤ) := by rw [Int.even_iff]; omega
  set m : ℤ := (q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * k with hm
  set n : ℤ := (p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * k with hn
  have hA : rayParam x y m n = (A : ℤ) := by
    simp only [rayParam, hm, hn]; linear_combination (A : ℤ) * hdet
  have hkk : (q : ℤ) * n - (p : ℤ) * m = (k : ℤ) := by
    simp only [hm, hn]; linear_combination (k : ℤ) * hdet
  have hsum : m + n = ((p : ℤ) + q) * (A : ℤ) + (x + y) * (k : ℤ) := by
    have h := sum_eq_ray hdet m n
    rwa [hA, hkk] at h
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hc, -⟩
    have hcop := (isCoprime_ray_iff hdet m n).mp hc
    rw [hA, hkk] at hcop
    have hg : Int.gcd (A : ℤ) (k : ℤ) = 1 := Int.isCoprime_iff_gcd_eq_one.mp hcop
    have hnat : Nat.Coprime A k := by simpa [Int.gcd_natCast_natCast] using hg
    exact hnat.symm
  · intro hc
    have hcop : IsCoprime ((A : ℤ)) ((k : ℤ)) := by
      rw [Int.isCoprime_iff_gcd_eq_one]
      simpa [Int.gcd_natCast_natCast] using hc.symm
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [isCoprime_ray_iff hdet, hA, hkk]; exact hcop
    · rw [hsum]
      exact parity_free_of_even_charge (x := x) (y := y) hpq hkeven hcop

open scoped Classical in
/-- **Brightness of a ray, both-odd case.** Let `p, q` be odd and let `k` be an odd charge.
Then, in any window of `2k` consecutive ray parameters, exactly `2 φ(k)` give Berggren nodes:
the ray has linear node density `φ(k)/k`. In particular the unit rays `k = 1` are completely
full, and a ray of prime charge `r` has density `1 - 1/r`. -/
theorem ray_census_both_odd {p q : ℕ} (hp : p % 2 = 1) (hq : q % 2 = 1) {x y : ℤ}
    (hdet : (q : ℤ) * x - (p : ℤ) * y = 1) {k : ℕ} (hk : k % 2 = 1) (a : ℕ) :
    #((Finset.Ico a (a + 2 * k)).filter (fun A : ℕ =>
        IsCoprime ((q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * k) ((p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * k) ∧
          Odd (((q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * k) + ((p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * k)))) = 2 * Nat.totient k := by
  rw [Finset.filter_congr (fun A _ => node_iff_coprime_of_both_odd hp hq hdet hk A),
    window_coprime_card]

open scoped Classical in
/-- **Brightness of a ray, even-charge case.** When `p + q` is odd and the charge `k` is even,
the same law holds: `2 φ(k)` nodes per window of `2k` ray parameters. -/
theorem ray_census_even_charge {p q : ℕ} (hpq : (p + q) % 2 = 1) {x y : ℤ}
    (hdet : (q : ℤ) * x - (p : ℤ) * y = 1) {k : ℕ} (hk : k % 2 = 0) (a : ℕ) :
    #((Finset.Ico a (a + 2 * k)).filter (fun A : ℕ =>
        IsCoprime ((q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * k) ((p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * k) ∧
          Odd (((q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * k) + ((p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * k)))) = 2 * Nat.totient k := by
  rw [Finset.filter_congr (fun A _ => node_iff_coprime_of_even_charge hpq hdet hk A),
    window_coprime_card]

/-- **Unit rays are completely full.**  Specialising the brightness law to `k = 1`: every one of
the `2` ray parameters in a window of length `2` gives a Berggren node.  This is the sharpest
form of "the brightest radial lines are the ones of charge `±1`". -/
theorem unit_ray_full {p q : ℕ} (hp : p % 2 = 1) (hq : q % 2 = 1) {x y : ℤ}
    (hdet : (q : ℤ) * x - (p : ℤ) * y = 1) (a : ℕ) :
    #((Finset.Ico a (a + 2 * 1)).filter (fun A : ℕ =>
        IsCoprime ((q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ)) ((p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
          Odd (((q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ))
            + ((p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ))))) = 2 := by
  classical
  rw [ray_census_both_odd hp hq hdet (k := 1) (by norm_num) a]
  simp

/-! ## Part 4. The third regime: half-brightness at mixed parity

The remaining case is `p + q` odd with an **odd** charge `k`.  Here the parity condition is not
automatic: it pins the ray parameter `A` to a *single residue class mod 2*, and the brightness
drops by exactly a factor of two, from `2 φ(k)` to `φ(k) = φ(2k)` nodes per window of `2k`.
This is the arithmetic shadow of the resolution law: at a star `p/q` with `p+q` odd the rays are
spaced `1/q` apart in `sinh`, twice as finely as at a both-odd star, and correspondingly each
individual ray is only half as bright. -/

/-- Parity along a ray in the mixed regime: with `p+q` odd and `k` odd, the node condition forces
the ray parameter into one fixed residue class mod `2`, determined by the parity of the Bezout
cofactor sum `x + y`. -/
theorem parity_mixed {p q : ℕ} (hpq : (p + q) % 2 = 1) {x y : ℤ} {k : ℕ} (hk : k % 2 = 1)
    (A : ℕ) :
    Odd (((p : ℤ) + q) * A + (x + y) * k) ↔ A % 2 = (if Even (x + y) then 1 else 0) := by
  have hpqodd : Odd ((p : ℤ) + q) := by
    have : Odd ((p + q : ℕ) : ℤ) := by rw [Int.odd_iff]; omega
    simpa using this
  have hkodd : Odd (k : ℤ) := by rw [Int.odd_iff]; omega
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hpqodd.sub_odd (odd_one (α := ℤ))
  obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := hkodd.sub_odd (odd_one (α := ℤ))
  have hdiff : Even ((((p : ℤ) + q) * A + (x + y) * k) - ((A : ℤ) + (x + y))) :=
    ⟨(A : ℤ) * c + (x + y) * d, by linear_combination (A : ℤ) * hc + (x + y) * hd⟩
  have hiff : Odd (((p : ℤ) + q) * A + (x + y) * k) ↔ Odd ((A : ℤ) + (x + y)) := by
    rw [← Int.not_even_iff_odd, ← Int.not_even_iff_odd, not_iff_not]
    exact Int.even_sub.mp hdiff
  rw [hiff]
  rcases Int.even_or_odd (x + y) with he | ho
  · rw [if_pos he]
    constructor
    · intro h
      have hAodd : Odd (A : ℤ) := by
        rcases Int.even_or_odd (A : ℤ) with h1 | h1
        · exact absurd h (by simp [Int.not_odd_iff_even, h1.add he])
        · exact h1
      have := Int.odd_iff.mp hAodd
      omega
    · intro h
      have hA : Odd (A : ℤ) := by rw [Int.odd_iff]; omega
      exact hA.add_even he
  · rw [if_neg (by simpa [Int.not_even_iff_odd] using ho)]
    constructor
    · intro h
      have hAeven : Even (A : ℤ) := by
        rcases Int.even_or_odd (A : ℤ) with h1 | h1
        · exact h1
        · exact absurd h (by simp [Int.not_odd_iff_even, h1.add_odd ho])
      have := Int.even_iff.mp hAeven
      omega
    · intro h
      have hA : Even (A : ℤ) := by rw [Int.even_iff]; omega
      exact hA.add_odd ho

/-- A window of `2k` consecutive integers (`k` odd) contains exactly `φ(k)` integers that are
coprime to `k` **and** of a prescribed parity: the parity condition halves the count. -/
theorem window_coprime_parity_card {k : ℕ} (hk : k % 2 = 1) (a e : ℕ) :
    #((Finset.Ico a (a + 2 * k)).filter (fun A : ℕ => Nat.Coprime k A ∧ A % 2 = e % 2))
      = Nat.totient k := by
  classical
  rw [← Nat.filter_coprime_Ico_eq_totient k a]
  refine (Finset.card_nbij' (i := fun B => if B % 2 = e % 2 then B else B + k)
    (j := fun A => if A < a + k then A else A - k) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_).symm
  · intro B hB
    simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Finset.mem_Ico] at hB ⊢
    obtain ⟨⟨h1, h2⟩, hc⟩ := hB
    by_cases hp : B % 2 = e % 2
    · rw [if_pos hp]; exact ⟨⟨by omega, by omega⟩, hc, hp⟩
    · rw [if_neg hp]
      exact ⟨⟨by omega, by omega⟩, Nat.coprime_add_self_right.mpr hc, by omega⟩
  · intro A hA
    simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Finset.mem_Ico] at hA ⊢
    obtain ⟨⟨h1, h2⟩, hc, hpar⟩ := hA
    by_cases hlt : A < a + k
    · rw [if_pos hlt]; exact ⟨⟨h1, hlt⟩, hc⟩
    · rw [if_neg hlt]
      have hAk : A - k + k = A := by omega
      refine ⟨⟨by omega, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
      exact (Nat.coprime_add_self_right (m := k) (n := A - k)).mp (by rwa [hAk])
  · intro B hB
    simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Finset.mem_Ico] at hB
    obtain ⟨⟨h1, h2⟩, hc⟩ := hB
    by_cases hp : B % 2 = e % 2
    · simp only [if_pos hp, if_pos h2]
    · simp only [if_neg hp]
      rw [if_neg (by omega)]
      omega
  · intro A hA
    simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Finset.mem_Ico] at hA
    obtain ⟨⟨h1, h2⟩, hc, hpar⟩ := hA
    by_cases hlt : A < a + k
    · simp only [if_pos hlt, if_pos hpar]
    · simp only [if_neg hlt]
      rw [if_neg (by omega)]
      omega

/-- Node characterisation in the mixed regime. -/
theorem node_iff_of_mixed {p q : ℕ} (hpq : (p + q) % 2 = 1) {x y : ℤ}
    (hdet : (q : ℤ) * x - (p : ℤ) * y = 1) {k : ℕ} (hk : k % 2 = 1) (A : ℕ) :
    (IsCoprime ((q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * k) ((p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * k) ∧
      Odd (((q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * k) + ((p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * k))) ↔
      (Nat.Coprime k A ∧ A % 2 = (if Even (x + y) then 1 else 0) % 2) := by
  have he2 : (if Even (x + y) then 1 else 0) % 2 = (if Even (x + y) then 1 else 0) := by
    split_ifs <;> rfl
  rw [he2]
  set m : ℤ := (q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * k with hm
  set n : ℤ := (p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * k with hn
  have hA : rayParam x y m n = (A : ℤ) := by
    simp only [rayParam, hm, hn]; linear_combination (A : ℤ) * hdet
  have hkk : (q : ℤ) * n - (p : ℤ) * m = (k : ℤ) := by
    simp only [hm, hn]; linear_combination (k : ℤ) * hdet
  have hsum : m + n = ((p : ℤ) + q) * (A : ℤ) + (x + y) * (k : ℤ) := by
    have h := sum_eq_ray hdet m n
    rwa [hA, hkk] at h
  have hcopiff : IsCoprime m n ↔ Nat.Coprime k A := by
    rw [isCoprime_ray_iff hdet, hA, hkk, Int.isCoprime_iff_gcd_eq_one]
    constructor
    · intro hg
      have hnat : Nat.Coprime A k := by simpa [Int.gcd_natCast_natCast] using hg
      exact hnat.symm
    · intro hc
      simpa [Int.gcd_natCast_natCast] using hc.symm
  rw [hcopiff, hsum, parity_mixed hpq hk A]

open scoped Classical in
/-- **Brightness of a ray, mixed regime (half-brightness).** When `p + q` is odd and the charge
`k` is odd, a window of `2k` ray parameters carries exactly `φ(k) = φ(2k)` Berggren nodes —
half of the `2 φ(k)` of the other two regimes.  This completes the trichotomy of the brightness
law and explains, together with the resolution law, the two visually distinct kinds of star. -/
theorem ray_census_mixed {p q : ℕ} (hpq : (p + q) % 2 = 1) {x y : ℤ}
    (hdet : (q : ℤ) * x - (p : ℤ) * y = 1) {k : ℕ} (hk : k % 2 = 1) (a : ℕ) :
    #((Finset.Ico a (a + 2 * k)).filter (fun A : ℕ =>
        IsCoprime ((q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * k) ((p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * k) ∧
          Odd (((q : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + y * k) + ((p : ℤ) * (A : ℤ) + x * k))))
      = Nat.totient k := by
  rw [Finset.filter_congr (fun A _ => node_iff_of_mixed hpq hdet hk A),
    window_coprime_parity_card hk a]

`k`-th and `(k+1)`-st node of the corresponding path from the root. The Cesàro mean

from __future__ import annotations

from math import acosh, asinh, cosh, gcd, isqrt, log, sinh, sqrt
from typing import Dict, Iterator, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

Seed = Tuple[int, int]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Seeds, tree moves, embedding
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def is_seed(m: int, n: int) -> bool:
    """Euclid seed: 0 < n < m, coprime, opposite parity."""
    return 0 < n < m and gcd(m, n) == 1 and (m + n) % 2 == 1


def seeds_up_to(mmax: int) -> List[Seed]:
    """All Euclid seeds with m <= mmax, in lexicographic order."""
    return [(m, n) for m in range(2, mmax + 1) for n in range(1, m) if is_seed(m, n)]


def triple(m: int, n: int) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
    """The primitive Pythagorean triple seeded by (m, n)."""
    return (m * m - n * n, 2 * m * n, m * m + n * n)


def berggren_children(s: Seed) -> Tuple[Seed, Seed, Seed]:
    """The three Berggren moves in seed coordinates."""
    m, n = s
    return ((2 * m - n, m), (2 * m + n, m), (m + 2 * n, n))


def berggren_parent(s: Seed) -> Optional[Seed]:
    """Inverse of the tree: the parent of a non-root seed, by the slope trichotomy."""
    m, n = s
    if (m, n) == (2, 1):
        return None
    if m > 3 * n:
        return (m - 2 * n, n)
    if m > 2 * n:
        return (n, m - 2 * n)
    return (n, 2 * n - m)


def depth(s: Seed) -> int:
    """Depth of a seed in the Berggren tree (root (2,1) has depth 0)."""
    d = 0
    cur: Optional[Seed] = s
    while cur is not None and cur != (2, 1):
        cur = berggren_parent(cur)
        d += 1
    return d


def embed(m: int, n: int) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """The half-plane point z(m,n) = (n + i)/m as (Re, Im)."""
    return (n / m, 1.0 / m)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hyperbolic geometry
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def hyp_radius(m: int, n: int) -> float:
    """d(i, z(m,n)) = arcosh((m^2 + n^2 + 1)/(2m))."""
    return acosh((m * m + n * n + 1) / (2 * m))


def hyp_dist_nodes(m1: int, n1: int, m2: int, n2: int) -> float:
    """Exact distance between two nodes: cosh d = ((n1 m2 - n2 m1)^2 + m1^2 + m2^2)/(2 m1 m2)."""
    cross = n1 * m2 - n2 * m1
    return acosh((cross * cross + m1 * m1 + m2 * m2) / (2 * m1 * m2))


def hyp_dist_numeric(z1: Tuple[float, float], z2: Tuple[float, float]) -> float:
    """Distance from the general half-plane formula, for cross-checking."""
    (x1, y1), (x2, y2) = z1, z2
    sq = (x1 - x2) ** 2 + (y1 - y2) ** 2
    return acosh(1.0 + sq / (2.0 * y1 * y2))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Star charges, resolution, brightness
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def star_charge(p: int, q: int, m: int, n: int) -> int:
    """k(p,q; m,n) = q n - p m."""
    return q * n - p * m


def hypercycle_width(p: int, q: int, m: int, n: int) -> float:
    """d(z(m,n), geodesic over p/q) = arsinh(|k|/q)."""
    return asinh(abs(star_charge(p, q, m, n)) / q)


def star_gap(p: int, q: int) -> int:
    """1 if p+q is odd, 2 if p and q are both odd."""
    return 1 if (p + q) % 2 == 1 else 2


def resolution(p: int, q: int) -> float:
    """delta(p/q) = gap(p,q)/q."""
    return star_gap(p, q) / q


def visible_rationals(threshold: float, qmax: int = 40) -> List[Tuple[int, int, float]]:
    """All p/q in [0,1] with delta(p/q) >= threshold, sorted by decreasing delta."""
    out: List[Tuple[int, int, float]] = []
    for q in range(1, qmax + 1):
        for p in range(0, q + 1):
            if gcd(p, q) != 1:
                continue
            d = resolution(p, q)
            if d >= threshold - 1e-12:
                out.append((p, q, d))
    out.sort(key=lambda t: (-t[2], t[1], t[0]))
    return out


def bezout(p: int, q: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """Integers x, y with q x - p y = 1 (requires gcd(p,q) = 1)."""
    # extended Euclid on (q, p): q*a + p*b = 1, then x = a, y = -b.
    old_r, r = q, p
    old_a, a = 1, 0
    old_b, b = 0, 1
    while r != 0:
        quo = old_r // r
        old_r, r = r, old_r - quo * r
        old_a, a = a, old_a - quo * a
        old_b, b = b, old_b - quo * b
    assert old_r == 1, "p and q must be coprime"
    return old_a, -old_b


def ray_node(p: int, q: int, x: int, y: int, big_a: int, k: int) -> Seed:
    """The lattice point of ray parameter A and charge k."""
    return (q * big_a + y * k, p * big_a + x * k)


def totient(k: int) -> int:
    """Euler's totient."""
    if k == 0:
        return 0
    result, kk, d = k, k, 2
    while d * d <= kk:
        if kk % d == 0:
            while kk % d == 0:
                kk //= d
            result -= result // d
        d += 1
    if kk > 1:
        result -= result // kk
    return result


def ray_census(p: int, q: int, k: int, a: int = 0) -> int:
    """Count of Euclid seeds among the 2k ray parameters A in [a, a + 2k)."""
    x, y = bezout(p, q)
    count = 0
    for big_a in range(a, a + 2 * k):
        m, n = ray_node(p, q, x, y, big_a, k)
        if gcd(m, n) == 1 and (m + n) % 2 == 1:
            count += 1
    return count


def predicted_census(p: int, q: int, k: int) -> int:
    """The brightness law: 2 phi(k), except phi(k) in the mixed regime."""
    both_odd = (p % 2 == 1) and (q % 2 == 1)
    if both_odd or k % 2 == 0:
        return 2 * totient(k)
    return totient(k)

# Realisation of a charge, balls, collisions
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def realise_charge(p: int, q: int, k: int, j: int = 0) -> Seed:
    """The SL2(Z) construction: a seed of charge exactly k at p/q."""
    x, y = bezout(p, q)
    big_a = 1 + k * (x + y) + 2 * k * k * j
    return ray_node(p, q, x, y, big_a, k)


def ball_count(radius: float) -> int:
    """#{seeds : d(i, z) <= R}, via the circle theorem."""
    c, s = cosh(radius), sinh(radius)
    total = 0
    for m in range(1, int(c + s) + 1):
        rhs = s * s - (m - c) ** 2
        if rhs < 0:
            continue
        nmax = min(m - 1, int(sqrt(rhs)))
        for n in range(1, nmax + 1):
            if is_seed(m, n):
                total += 1
    return total


def two_square_seeds(nn: int) -> List[Seed]:
    """All Euclid seeds with m^2 + n^2 = N."""
    out: List[Seed] = []
    m = isqrt(nn)
    while m * m * 2 > nn:
        rest = nn - m * m
        n = isqrt(rest)
        if n * n == rest and is_seed(m, n):
            out.append((m, n))
        m -= 1
    return out


def euler_factor(nn: int, s1: Seed, s2: Seed) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """Euler's two-representation factorisation from a hypotenuse collision."""
    (m1, n1), (m2, n2) = s1, s2
    g = gcd(nn, m1 * m2 + n1 * n2)
    h = gcd(nn, m1 * n2 + n1 * m2)
    return (g, h)

",
    "collision_geometry": """"
Collision geometry: why the Pythagorean star map cannot factor.

A number N with two essentially different representations N = m1^2 + n1^2 =
m2^2 + n2^2 as a sum of two squares can be factored by Euler's method: with the
pivot P = m1 m2 + n1 n2,

        gcd(N, P) * gcd(N, m1 n2 + n1 m2) = N ,

both factors non-trivial.  Two such representations are two nodes of the
Berggren tree with the same hypotenuse -- a *collision* -- and both sit at
hyperbolic radius (1/2) log N + O(1) from the base point i.  This script tests
the two geometric obstructions that stop this from becoming an attack:

  (a) the separation law     d(z1, z2) >= log g - log 2,  g = gcd(N, P):
      the more informative the collision, the further apart its two witnesses;
      and for a balanced factorisation (N <= g^2) the witnesses are essentially
      antipodal, d >= (1/2) log N - log 2;

  (b) the counting law       #{nodes within distance R of i} = Theta(e^{2R}),
      so the smallest ball guaranteed to contain a collision for N -- radius
      about (1/2) log N + log 2 -- already contains Theta(N) nodes.

Every printed inequality is asserted, so a failure would be loud.

Run:  python3 collision_geometry.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from math import acosh, cosh, gcd, isqrt, log, sinh, sqrt
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

Seed = Tuple[int, int]


def is_seed(m: int, n: int) -> bool:
    return 0 < n < m and gcd(m, n) == 1 and (m + n) % 2 == 1


def hyp_radius(m: int, n: int) -> float:
    return acosh((m * m + n * n + 1) / (2 * m))


def hyp_dist_nodes(m1: int, n1: int, m2: int, n2: int) -> float:
    cross = n1 * m2 - n2 * m1
    return acosh((cross * cross + m1 * m1 + m2 * m2) / (2 * m1 * m2))


def two_square_seeds(nn: int) -> List[Seed]:
    """All Euclid seeds (m, n) with m^2 + n^2 = N."""
    out: List[Seed] = []
    m = isqrt(nn)
    while m * m * 2 > nn:
        rest = nn - m * m
        n = isqrt(rest)
        if n * n == rest and is_seed(m, n):
            out.append((m, n))
        m -= 1
    return out


def euler_pair(nn: int, s1: Seed, s2: Seed) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
    """Pivot P and the two Euler factors g, h with g*h = N."""
    (m1, n1), (m2, n2) = s1, s2
    pivot = m1 * m2 + n1 * n2
    g = gcd(nn, pivot)
    h = gcd(nn, m1 * n2 + n1 * m2)
    return pivot, g, h


def ball_count(radius: float) -> int:
    """Nodes within hyperbolic distance R of i, via the circle theorem."""
    c, s = cosh(radius), sinh(radius)
    total = 0
    for m in range(1, int(c + s) + 1):
        rhs = s * s - (m - c) ** 2
        if rhs < 0:
            continue
        nmax = min(m - 1, int(sqrt(rhs)))
        for n in range(1, nmax + 1):
            if is_seed(m, n):
                total += 1
    return total


def survey(limit: int) -> None:
    """All odd N <= limit with at least two primitive two-square representations."""
    print(f"{'N':>7} {'seeds':>26} {'P':>8} {'g':>6} {'h':>6} "
          f"{'d(z1,z2)':>9} {'log g - log2':>12} {'slack':>7} {'balanced':>9}")
    rows = 0
    worst_slack = None
    for nn in range(5, limit + 1, 2):
        reps = two_square_seeds(nn)
        if len(reps) < 2:
            continue
        s1, s2 = reps[0], reps[1]
        pivot, g, h = euler_pair(nn, s1, s2)
        assert g * h == nn and 1 < g < nn, (nn, g, h)
        d = hyp_dist_nodes(*s1, *s2)
        bound = log(g) - log(2.0)
        slack = d - bound
        assert slack >= -1e-9, (nn, d, bound)
        balanced = nn <= g * g
        if balanced:
            assert d >= 0.5 * log(nn) - log(2.0) - 1e-9
        if worst_slack is None or slack < worst_slack[0]:
            worst_slack = (slack, nn)
        if rows < 22:
            print(f"{nn:>7} {str(s1) + ' ' + str(s2):>26} {pivot:>8} {g:>6} {h:>6} "
                  f"{d:>9.5f} {bound:>12.5f} {slack:>7.3f} {str(balanced):>9}")
        rows += 1
    print(f"\n  {rows} collisions with N <= {limit}; the separation bound held every time.")
    if worst_slack is not None:
        print(f"  tightest case: N = {worst_slack[1]}, slack = {worst_slack[0]:.4f}")


def radial_closeness(limit: int) -> None:
    """Colliding nodes are radially close: radii differ by at most 2 log 2."""
    worst = 0.0
    arg = 0
    for nn in range(5, limit + 1, 2):
        reps = two_square_seeds(nn)
        if len(reps) < 2:
            continue
        radii = [hyp_radius(m, n) for (m, n) in reps]
        spread = max(radii) - min(radii)
        assert spread <= 2 * log(2.0) + 1e-12
        if spread > worst:
            worst, arg = spread, nn
    print(f"\n  largest radial spread inside a collision fibre (N <= {limit}): "
          f"{worst:.5f} at N = {arg}")
    print(f"  guaranteed bound 2 log 2 = {2 * log(2.0):.5f}: never violated.")


def no_free_lunch() -> None:
    """The ball that must contain a collision already contains Theta(N) nodes."""
    print(f"\n{'N':>9} {'R = (1/2)logN + log2':>21} {'#nodes in ball':>15} "
          f"{'#nodes / N':>11}")
    for nn in [65, 325, 1105, 5525, 27625, 138125]:
        radius = 0.5 * log(nn) + log(2.0)
        cnt = ball_count(radius)
        print(f"{nn:>9} {radius:>21.5f} {cnt:>15} {cnt / nn:>11.4f}")
    print("  the count grows linearly in N: hyperbolic search inspects as many")
    print("  candidates as trial enumeration would, so there is no shortcut.")


def main() -> None:
    print("=" * 96)
    print("COLLISION GEOMETRY OF THE PYTHAGOREAN STAR MAP")
    print("=" * 96)
    survey(20000)
    radial_closeness(20000)
    no_free_lunch()
    print("\nAll asserted inequalities held.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

  * the hyperbolic circles d(i, .) = R, which by the circle theorem are the

  * the Pell spine, the orbit of the middle Berggren move, a genuine geodesic

def seeds(mmax: int) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
    return [(m, n) for m in range(2, mmax + 1) for n in range(1, m) if is_seed(m, n)]


def star_gap(p: int, q: int) -> int:
    """Charge spacing: 2 if p and q are both odd, else 1."""
    return 1 if (p + q) % 2 == 1 else 2

    "visualization_laws": """"
The two quantitative laws of the star map, side by side.

Left panel -- the RESOLUTION law.  For each rational p/q in [0,1] in lowest
terms, the angular resolution of its fan is

    delta(p/q) = gap(p,q) / q ,     gap = 2 if p, q both odd, else 1,

the minimal difference in sinh of the hyperbolic width between two rays that
carry nodes.  Plotted as a spike diagram over [0,1], with the visibility
threshold 2/5 marked: the spikes above it are exactly 0, 1/5, 1/3, 1/2, 3/5, 1.
Note the penalty on even denominators -- 1/4 falls below the line although
4 < 5.

Right panel -- the BRIGHTNESS law.  Along the ray of charge k, a window of 2k
consecutive ray parameters carries 2*phi(k) Berggren nodes (both-odd star, or
even charge) and phi(k) = phi(2k) in the mixed regime, so the linear density of
nodes on the ray is phi(k)/k or phi(k)/(2k).  Plotted against k, with the
measured density from a direct lattice scan overlaid as crosses.

Requires: matplotlib, numpy.  Writes starlaws.png.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from math import gcd
from typing import List, Tuple

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def star_gap(p: int, q: int) -> int:
    return 1 if (p + q) % 2 == 1 else 2


def resolution(p: int, q: int) -> float:
    return star_gap(p, q) / q


def totient(k: int) -> int:
    result, kk, d = k, k, 2
    while d * d <= kk:
        if kk % d == 0:
            while kk % d == 0:
                kk //= d
            result -= result // d
        d += 1
    if kk > 1:
        result -= result // kk
    return result


def bezout(p: int, q: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """x, y with q x - p y = 1."""
    old_r, r = q, p
    old_a, a = 1, 0
    old_b, b = 0, 1
    while r != 0:
        quo = old_r // r
        old_r, r = r, old_r - quo * r
        old_a, a = a, old_a - quo * a
        old_b, b = b, old_b - quo * b
    return old_a, -old_b


def measured_density(p: int, q: int, k: int) -> float:
    """Direct scan: fraction of ray parameters in [0, 2k) that give Euclid seeds."""
    x, y = bezout(p, q)
    hits = 0
    for big_a in range(0, 2 * k):
        m, n = q * big_a + y * k, p * big_a + x * k
        if gcd(m, n) == 1 and (m + n) % 2 == 1:
            hits += 1
    return hits / (2 * k)


def main() -> None:
    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14.0, 5.6))
    for ax in (ax1, ax2):
        ax.set_facecolor("#0a0f1f")

    qmax = 30
    pts: List[Tuple[float, float, int]] = []
    for q in range(1, qmax + 1):
        for p in range(0, q + 1):
            if gcd(p, q) == 1:
